subject: sea pig
title: Up to 600 of These 'Pigs' Herd Together Miles Under the Sea

scenes.text: There are pigs on the bottom of the ocean. They walk in herds.
Sea pigs live up to six thousand metres down. Some groups hold six hundred of them.
Here's the trick: they're sea cucumbers, walking on legs made of water.
They pump fluid in and out of tube feet, like stilts above the mud.
About one in five carries a passenger: a baby king crab hiding underneath.
They all face the current, sniffing for food that fell in the last hundred days.

description:
Sea pigs (Scotoplanes) are deep-sea cucumbers about 15 cm long that live 1,000 to 6,000 metres down and gather in groups of up to 600. They walk on tube feet by pumping fluid in and out.
About 22% are attended by juvenile king crabs, and they prefer freshly fallen food from roughly the last 100 days.
Would you rather meet a sea pig or a dumbo octopus?
first_comment: The baby crabs get a free ride and the sea pig gets nothing obvious out of it. What would you call a herd of sea pigs?
